verses.1: In the days when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land. A man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live in the fields of Moab. He went with his wife and his two sons.
verses.2: The name of the man was Elimelech, the name of his wife was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They went to live in the fields of Moab and remained there.
verses.3: Elimelech, the husband of Naomi, died. She was left with her two sons.
verses.4: They married two Moabite women. The name of one was Orpah, and the name of the second was Ruth. They lived there about ten years.
verses.5: Mahlon and Chilion also died. Naomi was left with no one—neither her husband nor her two sons.
verses.6: Naomi decided to return from the fields of Moab because she had heard in the fields of Moab that the Lord had remembered his people by giving them food.
verses.7: She left the place where she had been, and her two daughters-in-law went with her. They traveled along the road to return to the land of Judah.
verses.8: Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you to your mother’s house. May the Lord deal kindly with you as you have dealt kindly with the dead and with me.
verses.9: May the Lord provide a place for you where you may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband.” Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices and wept.
verses.10: They said to her, “We will certainly go back with you to your people.”
verses.11: Naomi said, “Return, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Do I still have sons in my womb who could become husbands for you?
verses.12: Return, my daughters. I am too old to have a husband. I have no hope that I will marry again and have children.
verses.13: Do you think I could wait for my sons to grow up? Or that you could stay unmarried? No, my daughters. It is very bitter for me because the Lord has dealt harshly with me.”
verses.14: They lifted up their voices and wept again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.
verses.15: Naomi said, “Look, your sister-in-law is returning to her people and to her gods. Return with her.”
verses.16: Ruth said, “Do not urge me to leave you or to return from following you. Wherever you go, I will go. Wherever you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.
verses.17: Wherever you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the Lord deal with me harshly if anything but death separates me from you.”
verses.18: Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, so she stopped trying to persuade her further.
verses.19: The two of them traveled together until they reached Bethlehem. When they arrived in Bethlehem, the whole town was stirred up at the sight of them, and they said, “Is this Naomi?”
verses.20: She said to them, “Do not call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.
verses.21: I went away full, but the Lord has brought me back empty. Why should you call me Naomi, since the Lord has afflicted me and the Almighty has caused me to suffer?”
verses.22: Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, went with her. They arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: "the days when the judges ruled" — the Hebrew phrase "בִּימֵי שְׁפֹט הַשֹּׁפְטִים" is translated as a dependent clause.
- v. 8: "the Lord deal kindly with you" — "חֶסֶד" is rendered as "kindly" to reflect its nuanced meaning of steadfast love or kindness.
- v. 16: "the Almighty" — "שַׁדַּי" is translated as "Almighty" to reflect its traditional theological connotation and to align with standard English Bible usage.
- v. 20-21: "Mara" — the Hebrew name "מָרָא" is directly translated as "Mara" to reflect Naomi’s changed identity.
raw:
[1] In the days when the judges ruled, there was a famine in the land. A man from Bethlehem in Judah went to live in the fields of Moab. He went with his wife and his two sons.

[2] The name of the man was Elimelech, the name of his wife was Naomi, and the names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. They were Ephrathites from Bethlehem in Judah. They went to live in the fields of Moab and remained there.

[3] Elimelech, the husband of Naomi, died. She was left with her two sons.

[4] They married two Moabite women. The name of one was Orpah, and the name of the second was Ruth. They lived there about ten years.

[5] Mahlon and Chilion also died. Naomi was left with no one—neither her husband nor her two sons.

[6] Naomi decided to return from the fields of Moab because she had heard in the fields of Moab that the Lord had remembered his people by giving them food.

[7] She left the place where she had been, and her two daughters-in-law went with her. They traveled along the road to return to the land of Judah.

[8] Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go back, each of you to your mother’s house. May the Lord deal kindly with you as you have dealt kindly with the dead and with me.

[9] May the Lord provide a place for you where you may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband.” Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices and wept.

[10] They said to her, “We will certainly go back with you to your people.”

[11] Naomi said, “Return, my daughters. Why would you come with me? Do I still have sons in my womb who could become husbands for you?

[12] Return, my daughters. I am too old to have a husband. I have no hope that I will marry again and have children.

[13] Do you think I could wait for my sons to grow up? Or that you could stay unmarried? No, my daughters. It is very bitter for me because the Lord has dealt harshly with me.”

[14] They lifted up their voices and wept again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth clung to her.

[15] Naomi said, “Look, your sister-in-law is returning to her people and to her gods. Return with her.”

[16] Ruth said, “Do not urge me to leave you or to return from following you. Wherever you go, I will go. Wherever you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.

[17] Wherever you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May the Lord deal with me harshly if anything but death separates me from you.”

[18] Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, so she stopped trying to persuade her further.

[19] The two of them traveled together until they reached Bethlehem. When they arrived in Bethlehem, the whole town was stirred up at the sight of them, and they said, “Is this Naomi?”

[20] She said to them, “Do not call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.

[21] I went away full, but the Lord has brought me back empty. Why should you call me Naomi, since the Lord has afflicted me and the Almighty has caused me to suffer?”

[22] Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabite, her daughter-in-law, went with her. They arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest.

Notes
- v. 1: "the days when the judges ruled" — the Hebrew phrase "בִּימֵי שְׁפֹט הַשֹּׁפְטִים" is translated as a dependent clause.
- v. 8: "the Lord deal kindly with you" — "חֶסֶד" is rendered as "kindly" to reflect its nuanced meaning of steadfast love or kindness.
- v. 16: "the Almighty" — "שַׁדַּי" is translated as "Almighty" to reflect its traditional theological connotation and to align with standard English Bible usage.
- v. 20-21: "Mara" — the Hebrew name "מָרָא" is directly translated as "Mara" to reflect Naomi’s changed identity.
